annotations.text: G — Marquee: type-led horizontal bands, no column split. Trade-off: the birds are reduced to an 88px photo strip, so nobody sees a face, a name or a price above the fold; the headline sells the brand, not the inventory. The type is also capped by the height gate: measured, the H1 wraps to a second line above 50px at 1440 and the artboard leaves the band.

H — Ledger hero: the hero IS the inventory, six real birds with prices and status. Trade-off: zero photography above the fold for a bird people buy on looks, and the rows go stale the day a bird sells, so this hero needs editing every clutch. At Mobile the ledger pushes the artboard well past a screen height.

I — Postcard: one wide photo card with the copy overlaid on a #0f3d2c scrim, credentials on a thin strip beneath. Trade-off: the scrim buries the lower third of the only photo, so the crop has to be chosen around the copy, and at Mobile the copy block grows until the photo is a thin banner over a dark panel.

Counter G · axis: UNDERLINE STAT. No card, no box, no bed. Newsreader numeral in ink #1f2a24 sitting on cream, a 3px clay #e8604c underline beneath it, then the label in 12px uppercase #5b524a. The four underlines run 68% / 100% / 54% / 34% of their column so the row reads as a mini bar chart. Mobile turns the chart on its side: four full-width rows, numeral left, label right, bar under each.
Trade-off: the bar lengths are typographic emphasis, not a measured scale. A reader can try to read them as data and ask what 34% of what means, and there is no axis to answer with. Longest of the three at Mobile (~284px root, ~236px of counter under the seam) because the sideways chart wants one row per stat.

Counter H · axis: SPLIT EMPHASIS. Asymmetric, never an equal 4-up. 12+ and 100% set at 58px forest #2D6A4F on the left; $1,500 and 24h stacked small at 24px ink on the right; exactly one 1px hairline (vertical at Desktop and Tablet, horizontal at Mobile) divides them. Shortest of the three at Tablet and second shortest at Desktop.
Trade-off: it demotes the two most transactional numbers on the strip. $1,500 Floor Price and 24h Reply Guarantee are the stats a buyer actually shops on, and this axis sets them at roughly 40% of the lead numerals, so credibility wins the squint test and the price does not.

Counter I · axis: STAMP ROW. Each stat inside a circular seal: 92px at Desktop, 84px Tablet, 72px Mobile, a 2px forest #2D6A4F ring with a 1px inner hairline, forest numeral centred, label beneath the circle. Circles, not rectangles. Most even height across the three viewports (200 / 196 / 198px root) because the badge size, not the copy, sets the height.
Trade-off: the seal shape reads as third-party certification, and all four of these are self-reported facts, which runs at CLAUDE.md rule 12. The circle also caps the numeral: $1,500 is the widest string and has to set at 24px inside a 92px badge, so the type scale is the flattest of the three (24/12 with no third step) and the strip leans on geometry rather than typography for hierarchy.
G — Arc gauge. A radial progress ring carries the position; the 4 parts sit beneath with counts. Trade-off: the ring costs vertical space that the flat index (H) spends on labels.
H — Numbered index. No ring at all: 01–18 as a numbered index with part rules. Trade-off: reads as a table of contents, so it loses the at-a-glance sense of progress the gauge gives.

I — Dot matrix. All 18 sections as one 6×3 map, only the active section labelled. Shortest of the three (471–527px). Trade-off: 17 of 18 dots are unlabelled, so it only works for someone already oriented.
G — Drawer index. Sticky top bar opens a full-width drawer DOWNWARD with all 18 grouped by part. Trade-off: one extra tap before any section is reachable.
H — Two-tier rail. Part tabs plus the active part's section pills, both always visible. Trade-off: two rows of sticky chrome eat the most viewport of the three.

I — Segment stepper. One line: position, prev/next, and an 18-segment bar that is itself the control. Trade-off: each segment is a ~20px visual target inside a 44px hit area, so it is the least precise to aim at.

G — Comparison bars. Mobile stacks each of the 12 traits as a label plus two value rows in three registers: the five rows with a real scale (size, lifespan, talking ability, onset, price) get a mini-bar scaled inside that row, the five qualitative rows get a plain chip, lab sexing and paperwork get a tinted check chip, and an SVG check marks the leading value (Congo on talking ability, Timneh on onset and on price, both on lab sexing and paperwork). Desktop keeps classic columns with a tint bed behind the leading cell. Trade-off: it is by far the tallest of the three on Mobile, about 1,380px stacked, and the bars invite a numeric reading of a comparison that is only partly numeric, so the row rhythm is deliberately uneven and a skimmer can read 'longer bar' as 'better bird' when on size and onset it means neither.

H — Definition list. Mobile is a boxless dl: trait as a small-caps dt, Congo and Timneh as dd rows with a bold column prefix, no cards, no borders, no rules. Tablet adds hairlines, Desktop sets the same dl as two typographic columns of six traits with hairline rules. Trade-off: it is the quietest and the cheapest to scan vertically at about 1,180px stacked on Mobile, but with no bed, no tint and no marker there is zero visual verdict, so a buyer who wants to be told which Grey to pick has to read all 12 traits and decide alone.

I — Pick-first. Mobile opens with ONE summary card that answers the question outright (Choose Congo if… / Choose Timneh if…, each with its real price and its real birds) and hides all 12 rows behind a closed “See all 12 rows” disclosure; the Tablet board shows that same disclosure open so the rows are reviewable; Desktop is classic columns under a sticky summary bar. Trade-off: the shortest Mobile answer at about 630px stacked closed, but it buries the comparison one tap deep, which costs the crawlable-at-a-glance detail and forces us to commit to a recommendation in the breeder's own voice.
G — Comparison bars. Values as weighted chips. Note: neither sex 'wins' here, and the artboards deliberately mark no winner — the page's own point is that upbringing matters more than sex.
H — Definition list. Boxless dl, no cards or borders. Trade-off: the least scannable of the three when comparing two values directly.
I — Pick-first. Verdict card up front, the 3 rows behind a disclosure. Trade-off: hides the detail that buyers comparing sexes actually came for.
G — Comparison bars. Noise level reads as a 3-step bar across the four species; African Grey marked as our pick. Trade-off: tallest at Mobile (1,185px).
H — Definition list. Species as dt, the three attributes as dd rows. Shortest at Mobile (957px). Trade-off: four species in a row of prose is a lot of reading.
I — Pick-first. Opens with African Grey as the pick, other three behind a disclosure. Trade-off: reads as advocacy rather than comparison, on a table whose job is comparison.

G. Comparison bars. Every price is plotted on one $95 to $3,500 scale, so CONGO PAIR reads as the ceiling and FERTILE EGG as the floor without doing arithmetic; ranges show as a lighter segment. Trade-off: it is the tallest Mobile artboard of the three, because each of the 6 offerings needs a header, a bar and 3 chips, and a bar invites shopping on length alone rather than on what the price includes.

H. Definition list. Boxless typography at Mobile: breed as a small-caps term with the price right-aligned on the same line, attributes as bold-prefixed rows. Least ink and the shortest Mobile height of the three. Trade-off: with no card edges the eye can drift from one offering's price to the next breed while scrolling, and TOP PICK reads as a quiet text tag, not a badge.

I. Pick-first. Mobile opens on the verdict, CONGO GREY / BABY at $2,300–$2,500, and puts the other options behind See all 6 options; Desktop keeps a sticky summary bar so the pick and the CTA follow the scroll. Trade-off: a comparison shopper pays one tap to see the other 5 rows, and the verdict steers every reader to the most expensive single bird. Shown expanded here so the breeder can check all 6 rows; it ships collapsed.
G — Topic accordion. All 21 questions grouped under 4 topic headers. 909px at Mobile against the live section's 2,404px. Trade-off: no single answer is visible until you open one.

H — Tab panel. 4 tabs, fixed-height panel, one topic at a time. Shortest at Mobile (750px) and the height does not grow with the question count. Trade-off: needs JS, and 16 of 21 questions are hidden at any moment.

I — Dense index. All 21 questions on one screen as one-line rows, answer opens in place. 1,368px at Mobile: the longest of the three, and the honest cost of showing everything. Trade-off: nothing is answered until tapped.

G — Price ladder. The three tiers as an ascending ladder $185 → $350 → $750 with the crate photo as a right rail. Trade-off: the ladder indent implies the top rung is 'best', which is a price claim we are not making.
H — Tier compare. Three columns, four comparison rows, stacking to cards at Mobile. Most complete of the three. Trade-off: tallest at Mobile (946px).
I — Photo band. Photo band with the copy on a scrim, tiers as chips that expand. Trade-off: only one tier's detail is visible at a time, so the comparison has to be done from memory.
